## Findings
- claim-1: Schur functions are homogeneous of partition weight, and the Grassmannian quotient inherits this grading. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- claim-2: The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- claim-3: The requested corollary \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee} \] is an integral graded isomorphism; it preserves torsion subgroups and every degreewise rank.
## Strategy
Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\), and let \(\Omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}\). By accepted quotient conjugation and ideal correspondence,
\[
\Omega:J_v\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Since \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\), \(\Omega\) is graded and \(\Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+\). Therefore
\[
\Omega(A_+J_v)=\Omega(A_+)\Omega(J_v)=A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee},
\]
so \(\Omega\) induces an integral graded isomorphism
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Here the right-hand \(A_+\) in the requested display is understood as \(A^\vee_+\).

In each degree, this is an isomorphism of finitely generated abelian groups. Hence it preserves torsion subgroups (indeed all invariant factors) and preserves free \(\mathbb Z\)-rank degreewise. Thus every certified degreewise rank and torsion computation transfers to the conjugate case.

The requested target is established, conditional only on the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence results.

## Gaps
None for this formal corollary under those accepted premises.
